title: British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
summary: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

image.caption: Chicago-born Greer moved to the UK in 1986 and acquired dual citizenship around a decade later [FILE: February 2020]Image: Mark Thomas/i Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: Playwright and author Bonnie Greer died aged 77, her husband David Hutchins said on Wednesday in a statement to British media.
A celebrated writer born in Chicago who at first plied her trade in New York, Greer spent most of her adult life in the UK.
She took up dual citizenship and became a regular and prominent political commentator in Britain.

blocks.caption: Greer attended the Frankfurt book fair in 2019 at the height of the post-Brexit debate for a panel on the topicImage: DW/E. Grenier

blocks.text: What did Greer's husband say about her death?

Greer's widower Hutchins hailed her as "an acclaimed playwright, author, critic, cultural and political commentator whose intelligence, courage and distinctive voice made an enduring contribution to British cultural and public life."
Hutchins said his late wife had suffered succumbed to a brief illness.
He said those closest to Greer would remember her warmth, humor, generosity and extraordinary ability to bring people together.
"To me, she was my partner, confidante and inspiration, and I feel profoundly privileged to have shared my life with her," Hutchins said. The pair married in 1993, seven years after Greer emigrated.

blocks.caption: Greed became a prominent political commentator and activist in the UK [FILE: October 2017]Image: Jonathan Nicholson/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: Greer was born in Chicago in 1948, the eldest of seven children from a family of Mississippi sharecroppers.
Her familial exposure to the UK predated even her birth — her father Ben was stationed in Britain during World War II and had taken part in the D-Day landings.
She gravitated towards creative writing amid the civil rights movement in the US after a college professor told her he did not believe women should pursue a legal career.
Having studied theater in Chicago she moved to New York as a young aspiring writer.
Greer settled in the UK in 1986 and worked mainly in theater with women and ethnic minorities.

She acquired British citizenship in 1997 and wrote a series of successful radio plays aired on the BBC and musicals. Her 1993 play "Munda Negra" exploring mental health problems among black women won the Verity Bargate Award for best play.
Greer also became a frequent contributor to political and social debate in Britain, frequently appearing on topical shows like "Newsnight" and "Question Time".

Greer was a prominent supporter of Barack Obama and wrote a memoir and personal musical history in 2009 called "Obama Music." She also campaigned against the UK's exit from the EU, Brexit, and Donald Trump's first term as US president at around the same time.

She held a series of cultural roles, including being president of the Bronte Society, chancellor of Kingston upon Thames University in London, a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature, and a board member of the Royal Opera House and the London Film School.
